Ghanaian dancehall artiste Shatta Wale has appealed to his former partner, Shatta Michy, to put their past differences aside and work with him to secure a better future for their son, Majesty.
The musician expressed concern about videos and images of the boy selling orange juice under the sun at Aburi, describing the situation as painful and insisting that his son should have opportunities to develop his interest in technology.
Speaking in an interview on Afternoon Ride with Andy Dosty on Hitz FM , Shatta Wale said he had introduced Majesty to technology and bought several gadgets to support his learning, adding that his own childhood exposure to computers had influenced his interest in the sector.
He said he wanted both parents to work together to nurture the boy's potential, regardless of the circumstances surrounding their separation.
“I grew up with gadgets, that's why I am into tech and I know how to use computer and all those things. My kids know that, Majesty, I have bought a lot of things for him to learn,” he said.
Shatta Wale, however, suggested that bitterness over their past relationship was affecting the possibility of a better working relationship with Michy.
Despite their differences, he described his former partner as a good woman and said their separation should not make them enemies.
“Shatta Michy is a very nice woman that I met, I will always praise and give her that respect. She should have that patience that life is like that, you win some, you lose some. If we are not together, that doesn't mean we are enemies,” he stated.
The artiste said he felt particularly distressed whenever he saw Majesty selling orange juice in the sun at Aburi, arguing that the child should be given the necessary support to pursue other opportunities.
He urged Michy to put aside whatever disagreements they had experienced and focus on their son's welfare, stressing that the priority should be building a better future for him.
“Whatever that has happened in life has passed. What we are thinking about is the kid right now, so she should open her mind. She shouldn't go and sit in the sun,” he added.
Shatta Wale further recalled that his father had not raised him to endure such circumstances, even when the family was experiencing difficult times.
He said he wanted Majesty to benefit from the opportunities available to him, particularly in technology, and called for both parents to work together to make that possible.
